title: EngageAI Dedicated Capacity Discovery - Sizing & Failover
next_steps: Send dedicated capacity pricing and commitment tiers
Share network diagram and SOC2 summary
Schedule infra deep dive for next Tuesday (SE-led)
Run 72-hour pilot with 2 reserved GPUs and burst to hosted
action_items: Aisha: Send pricing spreadsheet and sample contract by 2025-05-22
Marcus: Prepare initial benchmark commands and small test harness by 2025-05-23
Sofia: Share current infra layout and egress/security constraints by 2025-05-21
summary: Discovery focused on sizing reserved GPU pools, isolation (VPC/on-prem), burst/fallback strategy to hosted, and expected scaling patterns. Customer wants predictable unit cost for peak chat and a fallback plan for preemption or planned maintenance. Security and SOC2/KMS questions came up; they requested network diagram and contract tiering.
transcript: [00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thank you for joining. We're on for about 40 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:08] Ravi (EngageAI): Hey, I'm Ravi, head of ML at EngageAI. We run real-time chat, mostly customer support workflows. Low latency is... important.
[00:16] Sofia (EngageAI): Sofia, infra lead - I look after network, VPCs, and security controls.
[00:20] Dan (EngageAI): Dan, CTO - mostly listening but want to understand cost/levers for committed capacity.
[00:26] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus here, I'll cover technical details around dedicated pools, autoscale, and failover patterns.

[00:40] Aisha: Great. At a high level, you're evaluating Redwood's hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference. Today we want to understand your traffic peaks, isolation needs, and how you'd like burst handled. Ravi, can you share traffic patterns?

[00:58] Ravi: Sure: typical baseline is 600 concurrent users, peaks up to ~2,800 during business hours. Average utterance 25 tokens, but we have some long form generation too. We're looking at 24/7 availability; spikes during marketing campaigns are the pain point.
[01:20] Marcus: When you say spikes, are they predictable bursts or sudden unknown spikes? Any patterns we can leverage for scheduled scale?
[01:29] Ravi: Mostly predictable around PST 10am and 2pm; but sometimes sudden when a campaign goes viral. We'd like a reserved baseline and ability to burst without data egress issues.
[01:42] Sofia: Important: we need VPC isolation and customer-managed keys. Also SOC2 compliance docs and audit logs - those are blockers for procurement.

[01:55] Aisha: Got it. We offer Redwood Dedicated with reserved GPU pools for baseline capacity, plus burst options that can fall back to Redwood Hosted when you run out of reserved nodes. Hosted fallbacks can be configured to avoid data retention, but we'll share the details and the SOC2 artefacts.
[02:12] Dan: How is cost modeled for the burst? Do we pay pay-as-you-go for the hosted fallback and does latency increase?

[02:21] Marcus: Burst to hosted is pay-as-you-go at published hosted rates; latency can be slightly higher due to routing and model variant differences. You can define policy: prefer reserved, then dedicated spillover within same region, then hosted as last resort. We can also pin model variants to match latency profiles.
[02:45] Ravi: Can you survive a fallback where models are quantized? We care about hallucination rate; quality variance matters.

[02:55] Marcus: Yes—quality is a tradeoff. You can set fallback to only compatible variants we certify to be close in perf/quality. Also we recommend a smoke-test routing that validates outputs before sending to production users.
[03:12] Sofia: Network wise, we need private endpoints. Do you support VPC peering and private link? Any ports to open?

[03:22] Marcus: We support VPC peering and private link, plus an on-prem package for air-gapped if needed. Minimal egress needed for control plane. We'll send a network diagram and firewall rules. There's occasionally confusion in our docs where "KV cache" was written as "K-V cash" in auto-transcripts, sorry for that, but it's just key-value runtime cache for prefix reuse.
[03:48] Ravi: How do you handle preemption/maintenance—if our reserved GPU goes down mid-day?

[03:55] Marcus: Reserved pools are SLA-backed. We offer multi-zone placement and proactive maintenance windows. If there's a hardware event, routing policy can move traffic to a standby within Dedicated or to Hosted. You can configure automatic retries, canary routes, or circuit-breaker style fallbacks.
[04:15] Dan: We want predictable tail latency. Is there token-level observability and per-route latency SLOs?
[04:22] Aisha: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level latency and cost breakdowns. You can set per-route SLOs and get alerts when regressions happen.
[04:30] Ravi: For sizing, what footprint do we expect per GPU for our chat model? We use an LLM ~7B fine-tuned for dialogue. approx 2-3k tokens per second?

[04:42] Marcus: For a 7B we typically see 60-100 tokens/sec per A100-ish GPU for generation workloads depending on batch and seq len. With batching and KV cache, effective throughput increases. For your 2,800 concurrent short requests, recommended starting point is 2 reserved GPUs with autoscale + 1 burstable slot, then validate with a pilot.
[05:05] Sofia: That feels low given our peak. Can you explain how batching reduces the GPU count?

[05:12] Marcus: Sure—continuous batching groups requests to improve utilization, meaning we can serve more QPS for similar cost. But latency targets constrain max batching window. If you need <200ms p95, batching is limited. If 300-500ms is acceptable, you get much better throughput.
[05:32] Ravi: Our acceptable p95 is 350ms for standard flows, 750ms for longer background generations. So there's some headroom.
[05:40] Dan: What about quantization? If we quantize to 4-bit, what's the quality delta?

[05:46] Marcus: Quantization can save 2-3x memory and cost but may slightly change outputs. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload; we can run QC tests against your eval prompts to estimate delta.
[05:58] Aisha: We should also cover deployment topology: single-tenant GPU pools vs multi-tenant nodes. Sofia, do you require single-tenant hardware?
[06:08] Sofia: For PII workloads, yes. We have customers with HIPAA data—need isolation. For chat PII we need dedicated GPUs and no co-tenancy.

[06:18] Marcus: Dedicated supports both single-tenant nodes and tenant-isolated pools. For strict isolation you'll want Dedicated with dedicated hosts and customer-managed KMS. For less stringent, reserved multi-tenant pools are available.
[06:32] Ravi: How quick is autoscaling for burst? We can't afford a slow cold-start during a viral spike.

[06:39] Marcus: Autoscale can be configured for proactive scaling based on predicted traffic, or reactive scale which takes a few minutes for GPU spin-up. For near-instant capacity we use warm standby capacity (burst nodes) kept warm but not charged at full rate—looks like a reserved burst model.
[06:55] Dan: Can we buy reserved baseline and keep a warm standby in same AZ for 20% extra cost?
[07:02] Aisha: Yes, that's a common pattern—reserved baseline + warm standby for critical endpoints. Pricing differs but it's cheaper than full reserved for the standby.
[07:10] Sofia: On security: SAML/SSO integration and audit logs—how granular are logs? We need token-level traces for compliance.
[07:18] Marcus: Audit logs include request ID, model variant, latency, tokens, and route decisions. We can retain logs per your retention policy as an add-on.
[07:28] Ravi: About data handling during hosted fallback—do you store prompts? Are they shared with other tenants?
[07:35] Marcus: Hosted fallback can be configured with no retention for your requests or with encryption keys you manage. We don't train on customer data; policies can be enforced in the contract.
[07:44] Dan: Procurement needs a rough cost example for budgeting. Can you give a back-of-envelope?

[07:50] Aisha: Sure—based on Marcus' sizing recommendation, 2 reserved GPUs plus warm standby and expected burst-to-hosted ~20% of traffic results in an estimated monthly run-rate. We'll send detailed tiers in the pricing sheet.
[08:02] Ravi: Would a 72-hour pilot make sense? We can route a sample subset to Dedicated and measure latency/costs.
[08:09] Marcus: That works. For pilot we configure two reserved GPUs, warm standby, and a small traffic slice. We'll supply benchmark harness and sample load scripts.
[08:20] Sofia: We will need the network/firewall egress list before we can enable the pilot. Also a contact for our security review.
[08:28] Aisha: I'll include that in the docs pack. Marcus, can you prepare the network diagram and the minimal firewall rules?

[08:34] Marcus: Yes, will do. Also I'll include sample curl commands and steps to run the eval harness. Note some of the docs still auto-transcribe product names wrong, e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes comes out as "Redwood dedicate" in captions so ignore that, ha.
[08:52] Ravi: (laughs) Fair. On SLAs, what uptime guarantees with Dedicated?
[08:58] Marcus: Dedicated comes with an SLA — 99.9% for availability depending on contract tier. We can discuss elevated SLAs for enterprise contracts.
[09:06] Dan: What about multi-region? If we fail a region, what's recovery?

[09:12] Marcus: We can provision dedicated pools in two regions and route with failover. That increases costs but provides region-level redundancy. Alternatively, use Hosted fallback in another region as last-resort.
[09:25] Ravi: For the pilot we'll stay single-region, but we care about production multi-region design.
[09:30] Sofia: Any data residency or crypto constraints? We use customer-managed KMS for secrets and HSM for keys in certain cases.
[09:37] Marcus: We integrate with common KMS providers and offer HSM integrations for Private deployments. We'll document supported providers.
[09:45] Aisha: Quick qualification—timeline and decision criteria?
[09:49] Ravi: We're targeting a pilot next week, procurement by mid-June. Decision hinges on predictable cost, isolation, and a clean security review.
[09:58] Dan: Also want low ops overhead for our small infra team.
[10:02] Marcus: Noted. We'll make the pilot low-touch and provide managed runbooks.
[10:10] Sofia: About monitoring - can Redwood forward metrics to our Prometheus/Grafana stack?
[10:15] Marcus: Yes, we have exporters and can stream metrics and traces to your observability. We'll share schema and sample configs.
[10:26] Ravi: Any important caveats with caching? We use prefix reuse heavily—does that affect billing?

[10:33] Marcus: KV cache reduces token consumption by avoiding regeneration of repeated prefixes. Billing is per token generated/consumed; effective token count goes down because of cache hits, so you save on cost.

[10:44] Aisha: Let's wrap with a recap and next steps. I'll go first: send pricing, SOC2 summary, network diagram, and contract draft. Marcus will run initial bench harness and provide pilot instructions. Sofia will share infra details.
[11:00] Ravi: We'll confirm pilot scope and provide sample prompts and traffic patterns. Dan will review procurement timeline.
[11:08] Marcus: I'll also add a short doc on recommended fallback policies and canary steps to validate quality on fallback.
[11:16] Aisha: Great. Any final questions?
[11:20] Dan: None from me. Thanks everyone.
[11:24] Sofia: Nope. Thanks, talk soon.
[11:27] Aisha: Thanks, we'll follow up with the pack by Friday. Meeting end.
[11:35] SYSTEM NOTE: Recording ended. Approx 42 minutes total (transcription trimmed).
